chapter: Mario Bauza and the Cuban sextets
title: Friendship with Mario; Sexteto Redencion and silent-movie theatre
summary: They became friends, Machito joined Sexteto Redencion while Mario worked at the Inglaterra Theatre accompanying silent films.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Okay. Macho try to think back to that time where you first saw Mario and your sister introduced him. What do you remember about that? - that incident.
Well, on account that I was a music
lover and Mario was a well-educated, musically, so to me was a good - a good thing because he wasn't somebody that, you know, that you don't know where he is from. He was an accomplished musician.
You already knew of him before you met him?
I knew about it - Oh yes
You knew about him enough. Okay, so your sister says: "This is Mario Bauza". What happened after that?
Well, they start to, you know.....
Did you start hanging out together?
Yes, he my house, he used to come to my house and talk and this and this and that.
What, what did you talk about as young men?

Well, about six or seven months after Mario, my sister introduced me to Mario, I start working in Havana with Sexteto Redencion. So Mario was working at the Inglaterra Theatre; in those days there was, there wasn't no movie - movietone. It was a silent........
Si., so he - they used to adapt the semi-classic or classic music to the - to the silent music.
I see, to the movie then.
To the movie then; so I was working with

a sextet, naturally, he was a different category musically, but he was my official brother-in-law, so we had a good relation. So we used to go together to the movies and we make a date to go to a ball game because his father was a manager of a professional ball team and we liked baseball, we liked boxing, so we used to have a tremendous relation.
